idea-plugin.name: TornadoInsight
idea-plugin.description:
TornadoInsight makes it easier to develop TornadoVM applications in IntelliJ IDEA. It checks TornadoVM kernels for unsupported Java features as you type, runs individual kernels on your TornadoVM installation to show what TornadoVM generates for them, and writes TornadoVM boilerplate for you through live templates. Experimentally, it can also ask an AI model to transform a Java method into a TornadoVM kernel.

What's New in 2.1.0

  • AI-assisted transformation (experimental, off by default): transforms a Java method into a TornadoVM kernel (Loop Parallel API, Kernel API or Tile API) with a local model server or the Claude API, checks it, optionally runs it against the method, and shows a diff before applying it.
  • Quick fixes for assert statements, unused system and native calls, throw, try/catch, throws clauses and kernels that return a value.
  • Dynamic inspection compiles its test program against every jar of the TornadoVM SDK, and copies the kernel's code with correct imports, type names and class-qualified references.

Static checks

While you edit a TornadoVM kernel (a method with @Parallel/@Reduce loops, or one that takes a KernelContext or TileContext), TornadoInsight underlines the Java features TornadoVM cannot compile and explains why in a tooltip. It checks the kernel and the helper methods it calls for:
  • data types TornadoVM cannot compile to device code
  • direct and indirect recursion
  • throw, try/catch and methods that declare exceptions
  • assert statements
  • native methods, and JDK system, I/O and reflection classes
  • calls into classes outside the JDK and the TornadoVM API
  • TaskGraph instances held in static fields
  • kernel methods that return a value instead of void
  • calls to helper methods that cannot be checked
The Inspector Guide tab of the TornadoVM tool window explains each restriction. Press Alt+Enter on a reported assert, unused system or native call, throw, try/catch, throws clause or non-void return type for a quick fix.

Dynamic inspection

Some problems only show up when TornadoVM compiles and runs a kernel. Select kernels in the TornadoVM tool window and click Run: TornadoInsight generates a small test program around each kernel, compiles it and runs it on your TornadoVM installation. The TornadoInsight Console shows whether the kernel ran and the kernel code TornadoVM generated for it (e.g. OpenCL C or CUDA), or the error it hit.

Live templates

Type an abbreviation in a Java editor and press Tab:
  • tg: a TaskGraph that transfers inputs, runs a task and transfers outputs back
  • tep: a TornadoExecutionPlan for a TaskGraph, in a try-with-resources block
  • tparallel: a kernel method with a @Parallel loop
  • tkernel: a kernel method that takes a KernelContext
  • ttile: a kernel method that takes a TileContext (TornadoVM 7.0.0+)
For example, tg inserts: 
TaskGraph taskGraph = new TaskGraph("s0")
        .transferToDevice(DataTransferMode.FIRST_EXECUTION, INPUTS)
        .task("t0", CLASS::METHOD, ARGS)
        .transferToHost(DataTransferMode.EVERY_EXECUTION, OUTPUTS);
The templates are offered in modules that use the TornadoVM API, and in any Java project when TORNADOVM_HOME points at a TornadoVM SDK. The Live Templates tab of the TornadoVM tool window lists them with a preview.

AI-assisted transformation (experimental)

Right-click a plain Java method and choose Transform into TornadoVM Kernel (AI)..., or press Alt+Enter on its name. Choose the Loop Parallel API, the Kernel API, the Tile API (TornadoVM 7.0.0+, CUDA devices), or Fastest (measured), which times a kernel for each and recommends one. Each answer is checked like a kernel in the editor and the problems go back to the model; optionally, each kernel is run with TornadoVM and compared with the method. A diff shows the result before it is applied, as one undoable step. It is off until you set up a model, because it sends your code to it.

Getting started

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2023.1 or newer
  • A TornadoVM SDK 2.2.0 or newer, for dynamic inspection (TornadoVM 6.0.0 and newer need TornadoInsight 1.6.0 or newer). Install it with SDKMAN! (sdk install tornadovm) or from tornadovm.org/downloads.
  • A JDK 21 or newer as the project JDK, matching the requirement of your TornadoVM SDK; a standard OpenJDK build, not a GraalVM one
  • For AI-assisted transformation, a local server with the OpenAI chat API (such as llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama or LM Studio), or a Claude API key

Point TornadoInsight at TornadoVM

TornadoInsight finds TornadoVM through the TORNADOVM_HOME environment variable, which must be visible to the IDE process. IDEs started from a launcher, the Dock or JetBrains Toolbox do not read shell files such as ~/.bashrc, so set it as follows (which tornado shows where your SDK is):
  • Linux (systemd): create ~/.config/environment.d/tornado.conf containing TORNADOVM_HOME=/absolute/path/to/tornado-sdk, then log out and back in.
  • macOS: run launchctl setenv TORNADOVM_HOME /absolute/path/to/tornado-sdk, then quit the IDE (Cmd+Q) and start it again.
  • Windows: add a user variable TORNADOVM_HOME=C:\path\to\tornado-sdk under System Properties | Environment Variables, then restart the IDE.

Configure

Settings | Other Settings | TornadoInsight has one setting, Max array size: the length of the arrays (and the size of the other inputs) that dynamic inspection creates as test data. Dynamic inspection uses the project JDK from File | Project Structure. Settings | Other Settings | TornadoInsight | AI-Assisted Transformation enables the AI-assisted transformation and sets up its model: a local server or the Claude API.

For more information, see the TornadoInsight repository. The plugin is described in Dynamic and Static Code Analysis for Java Programs on Heterogeneous Hardware (MPLR '25, doi:10.1145/3759426.3760984).
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 2.1.0

  • AI-assisted transformation (experimental, off by default): Transform into TornadoVM Kernel (AI)... in the editor menu, or Alt+Enter on a method name, transforms a Java method into a TornadoVM kernel with a local model server (OpenAI chat API) or the Claude API, set up in Settings | Other Settings | TornadoInsight | AI-Assisted Transformation.
    • Choose the Loop Parallel API, the Kernel API, the Tile API (TornadoVM 7.0.0+, CUDA devices), or Fastest (measured), which transforms it into each, times the kernels and recommends one.
    • Each answer is checked like a kernel in the editor; problems go back to the model, for up to three answers.
    • Optionally, each kernel is run with TornadoVM and compared with the method, on this machine; it is off until you tick it.
    • A diff preview; Accept adds the kernel beside the method or replaces it, as one undoable step.
  • Quick fixes (Alt+Enter) for the static checks: remove an assert statement, an unused system or native call, a throw statement or a throws clause; unwrap a try/catch; make a kernel return void.
  • Dynamic inspection fixes: the test program is compiled against every jar of the TornadoVM SDK, and the copied kernel code gets correct imports and type names, and class-qualified references rewritten.

Version 2.0.0

  • Live templates: tg (TaskGraph), tep (TornadoExecutionPlan), and the kernel templates tparallel (@Parallel loop), tkernel (KernelContext) and ttile (TileContext, TornadoVM 7.0.0+). They are offered in modules that use the TornadoVM API, and in any Java project when TORNADOVM_HOME points at a TornadoVM SDK. A new Live Templates tab in the TornadoVM tool window lists them with a preview.
  • TileContext kernels are detected as TornadoVM tasks.
  • Static checks:
    • New: Non-void return type and Unanalysable helper checks.
    • The recursion check is faster, follows calls across classes, and reports each cycle once.
    • Calls to your own helper methods are no longer reported as external library calls, and unresolved types are no longer reported as unsupported data types.
    • The inspections are grouped under TornadoVM in the inspection settings.
  • Dynamic inspection:
    • Runs as a background task with progress, Cancel and timeouts.
    • Generates test data for every supported kernel parameter type, and runs KernelContext and TileContext kernels with a GridScheduler.
    • Clearer results: compile errors are summarised, and device limitations (e.g. no FP64) are reported as warnings instead of errors.
  • Task list: kept per project, refreshed while you edit, and no longer lost while the IDE is indexing.
  • Fixes: the Settings links open the TornadoInsight page, the max array size field no longer throws on non-numeric input, error reports build a correct GitHub issue link, and notifications use their own group.
  • New icons, matching the TornadoVM logo.
  • Removed: the TornadoVM bytecode visualizer, and the debug options in the settings.
  • Requires IntelliJ IDEA 2023.1 or newer.

Version 1.6.0

  • TornadoVM 6.0.0 compatibility: The JDK compatibility check now reads the etc/tornado.jdk contract that TornadoVM 6.0.0 ships (minimum JDK plus preview flag) instead of the removed tornado --version JDK marker, and accepts any project JDK at or above that minimum.
  • GraalVM JDK guard: A GraalVM project JDK is detected and reported with a clear error instead of a JVM crash, since TornadoVM 6.0.0+ bundles its own Graal compiler and JVMCI.
  • The info console reports the resolved TornadoVM JDK requirement and the project JDK in use.

Version 1.4.2

  • Environment Variable Update: The required environment variable has been renamed from TORNADO_SDK to TORNADOVM_HOME to align with TornadoVM's updated naming conventions. Please update your environment configuration accordingly.

Version 1.4.0

  • TornadoVM 2.0+ Support: Full compatibility with TornadoVM 2.0 and later versions
  • Automatic SDK Detection: The plugin now automatically detects your installed TornadoVM SDK without requiring manual configuration of the TornadoVM root directory
  • Streamlined Setup: No longer requires building TornadoVM from source - works directly with installed TornadoVM SDK packages
  • Improved Configuration: Simplified settings panel without explicit declaration of the Java SDK path. Instead, the plugin reuses the user-defined Java SDK from Project Settings
